messages.text: Wade and Aspinall make statement ahead of World Grand Prix semi-finals

metadata.summary: James Wade and Nathan Aspinall put in statement performances that will have made their semi-final opponents take note ahead of a mouthwatering Saturday night line-up at the World Grand Prix.
metadata.content: World Grand Prix Darts: James Wade and Nathan Aspinall with statement displays ahead of semi-finals | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content World Grand Prix Darts: James Wade and Nathan Aspinall with statement displays ahead of semi-finals James Wade faces Luke Humphries in final four after dropping just one leg in win over Gian van Veen; Nathan Aspinall averages 105.15 to set up Gerwyn Price meeting; watch the World Grand Prix semi-finals live on Saturday, from 8pm on Sky Sports+, 8.30pm on Main Event Saturday 3 October 2026 00:07, UK Image: James Wade will face Luke Humphries in the semi-finals of the World Grand Prix on Saturday James Wade and Nathan Aspinall put in statement performances that will have made their semi-final opponents take note ahead of a mouthwatering Saturday night line-up at the World Grand Prix. Aspinall threatened to set a new tournament record average when storming to a 3-0 win over Ryan Joyce, his 105.15 mark ultimately landing as the fourth-highest in history and the best-ever in a quarter-final. Wade, meanwhile, dropped only one leg as he, in his words, "bashed up" world No 2 Gian van Veen in a match that lasted little more than 20 minutes. metadata.summary: Manchester City’s strategy in their bid to clear their name after being found guilty of breaking more than 100 of the Premier League's rules has been brought into question by a statement their main sponsor Etihad Airways submitted to the US government in 2015.
metadata.content: Man City appeal: Club's strategy brought into question by 2015 statement main sponsor Etihad Airways submitted to US government | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Man City appeal: Club's strategy brought into question by 2015 statement main sponsor Etihad Airways submitted to US government Man City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission; City deny all charges and have lodged an appeal against the verdict; City were charged by the Premier League with more than 100 breaches in February 2023 By Zinny Boswell and Kaveh Solhekol Friday 2 October 2026 23:00, UK Manchester City’s strategy in their bid to clear their name after being found guilty of breaking more than 100 of the Premier League's rules has been brought into question by a statement their main sponsor Etihad Airways submitted to the US government in 2015. Sky Sports News understands that City are expected to argue as part of their appeal that the extra funding for their sponsorship deals came from the Abu Dhabi government and not the club's majority owners, Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG). However, a statement Etihad submitted to the US Departments of Commerce, Transportation and State in May 2015 appears to contradict this explanation. metadata.summary: Novak Djokovic again appeared to struggle with fitness issues as he came from behind to avoid a second-round exit to world No 104 Yunchaokete Bu at the China Open on Friday.
metadata.content: China Open and Japan Open: Novak Djokovic, Aryna Sabalenka and Naomi Osaka all advance, as Katie Boulter knocked out | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content China Open and Japan Open: Novak Djokovic, Aryna Sabalenka and Naomi Osaka all advance, as Katie Boulter knocked out Novak Djokovic sealed a second-round comeback win in Beijing as Naomi Osaka and Aryna Sabalenka both advanced; Katie Boulter was once again beaten by Karolina Muchova watch ATP Japan Open and WTA/ATP China Open this week live on Sky Sports Friday 2 October 2026 19:51, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Djokovic extended his winning run at the China Open to 31 matches Novak Djokovic again appeared to struggle with fitness issues as he came from behind to avoid a second-round exit to world No 104 Yunchaokete Bu at the China Open on Friday. The Serbian went 1-0 down before he was taken to a tiebreak in the second set. But Djokovic dug deep to claim the final set and cap off a resilient 4-6 7-6(7-2) 6-2 comeback victory over the Chinese wildcard, and extend his record winning streak at the China Open to 31 matches. messages.text: Jordan handles Piers Morgan 'sledging' to move into contention

metadata.summary: Matthew Jordan shot a seven-under 65 to move into contention at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship despite having to put up with Piers Morgan's verbal jousting.
metadata.content: Alfred Dunhill Links Championship: Matthew Jordan moves into contention with Casey Jarvis leading by one | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Alfred Dunhill Links Championship: Matthew Jordan moves into contention with Casey Jarvis leading by one Matthew Jordan survives 'sledging' from outspoken television presenter Piers Morgan to move into contention at Alfred Dunhill Links; South African Casey Jarvis leads by one on 11 under after a 67 at Kingsbarns Friday 2 October 2026 19:54, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day two of the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship. Matthew Jordan shot a seven-under 65 to move into contention at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship despite having to put up with Piers Morgan's verbal jousting. The Royal Liverpool member is looking for his first DP World Tour win in his 183rd tournament and he shrugged off the good-natured criticism from the television presenter - his amateur playing partner for the team part of the event - to card six birdies and an eagle at Carnoustie. His one mishap was a bogey at the ninth, his final hole, but he got to 10 under and into a four-way tie for second place.
